title: Scalar units and associators commute with the canonical balanced pullback comparison
statement:
For a scheme morphism q and normalized scalar models [def-sp-finite-free-direct-image-data], the canonical left balancing squares respect identity coefficients under the multiplication units, and respect arbitrary towers of coefficient maps under the specified derived scalar associators. The two component equations below are equations of left pullback functors and do not assert any direct-image isomorphism, input-shift compatibility or finite-basis statement.

theorem finiteFreeDirectImageBalancingCoherence {Z W : Scheme.{u}} (q : Z ⟶ W)
    (sW : ScalarModel W) (sZ : ScalarModel Z) :
    (∀ (R : Coefficients q) (K : DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules W R.target)),
      (proEtaleRingDerivedPullback q R.target R.source R.identification).map
          ((sW.unit R.target).inv.app K) ≫
        (balancing sW sZ (CoefficientMap.id R)).hom.app K ≫
        (sZ.unit R.source).hom.app
          ((proEtaleRingDerivedPullback q R.target R.source R.identification).obj K) = 𝟙 _) ∧
    (∀ (R S B : Coefficients q) (a : CoefficientMap R S) (b : CoefficientMap S B)
      (K : DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules W R.target)),
      (balancing sW sZ (a.comp b)).hom.app K =
        (proEtaleRingDerivedPullback q B.target B.source B.identification).map
          ((sW.normalization.derived a.target b.target).inv.app K) ≫
        (balancing sW sZ b).hom.app ((sW.presentation a.target).derived.obj K) ≫
        (sZ.presentation b.source).derived.map ((balancing sW sZ a).hom.app K) ≫
        (sZ.normalization.derived a.source b.source).hom.app
          ((proEtaleRingDerivedPullback q R.target R.source R.identification).obj K))

proof.text: Use flat-term K-flat resolutions to extend equality of natural transformations from resolving representatives. The derived Hom comparison gives an adjunction compatible with each universal scalar counit. Its unit equals the supplied scalar-model unit on flat-term K-flat representatives by the model normalization, hence everywhere. This identifies the supplied scalar adjunction with that Hom-comparison adjunction.

source.place: Tags 06YY, 07A6 and 0D6D; normalized scalar adjunctions and composition of inverse image.

proof.text: Transpose the ordinary balanced scalar associator under the composite ordinary adjunction. The ordinary unit formulas and the associator formula on 1 tensor (1 tensor x) show that its transpose is the composite-map unit. Thus it is the canonical adjunction composition comparison. The representative normalization of the derived associator and the preceding Hom comparison identify the derived associator with leftAdjointCompIso. Similarly, the multiplication formula on 1 tensor x and the universal derived unit normalization identify the supplied multiplication unit with leftAdjointIdIso.

source.place: Tags 06YY, 07A6 and 0D6D; normalized scalar adjunctions and composition of inverse image.

proof.text: The ordinary restriction/direct-image comparison, as well as the ordinary restriction composition comparisons, is the identity on sections. Their identity and tower equations follow by evaluation on sections. For the derived comparisons, use the universal right-derived unit to test equality, paste their specified normalization equations, and use naturality of that unit. The exact restriction composition and identity comparison normalization then reduce the pasted expressions to the ordinary equations.

source.place: Tags 06YY, 07A6 and 0D6D; normalized scalar adjunctions and composition of inverse image.

proof.text: Conjugation of isomorphisms preserves vertical composition and whiskering and sends unitors and associators to the corresponding right-adjoint unitors and associators. Conjugating the seven-factor tower with the three scalar adjunctions at each end reduces it to the preceding right-adjoint tower equation. Conjugating the multiplication-unit composite likewise reduces it to the right-adjoint identity equation. Substitute the normalized scalar identifications from the second step and evaluate the resulting natural isomorphisms on each object.
